class.name: DifferentialData
class.brief_description: Axle differential policy with locking percentages and coupling torque.
class.description: Open permits wheel-speed differences; Locked enforces equal wheel angular velocity without a finite torque cap. Limited Slip applies equal and opposite coupling torques to oppose wheel-speed differences. Its settings are hidden in the Inspector in other modes but remain saved. Numeric settings are copied into fixed runtime storage during setup; apply edits with [method Vehicle.restart]. Axle drive shares are normalized separately and there is no inter-axle differential.

members.member: Open, Limited Slip, or Locked. Limited-slip fields are only shown for Limited Slip mode.

Torque-driven locking effect when axle input torque and carrier velocity have the same sign, including reverse acceleration. The percentage is the supported wheel torque imbalance relative to total input torque, excluding preload, speed coupling, and the cap. Capacity contribution is abs(input torque) times percent divided by 200, because the correction adds to one wheel and subtracts from the other. At 40% and 100 Nm input, the torque-driven correction capacity is 20 Nm. A 100% setting is still finite and is not equivalent to Locked.

Torque-driven locking percentage when axle input torque and carrier velocity oppose one another, including reverse engine braking. Selection follows transmitted power rather than throttle or wheel-brake input. Uses the same percent/200 capacity conversion as acceleration locking.

Baseline limited-slip coupling capacity in Nm, including at zero input torque. Higher values resist wheel-speed differences more strongly during low-torque cornering. Capped by [member max_lock_torque].

Advanced cap on limited-slip coupling torque in Nm. Actual applied correction can be smaller than capacity. Total capacity is min(cap, preload + abs(input torque)*active_percent/200 + speed-dependent coupling). Inactive in Open and Locked modes.

Advanced additional coupling capacity in Nm for each 100 RPM difference between wheel speeds. This contributes even at zero input torque. Zero disables speed-dependent coupling. The sum of all contributions is capped by [member max_lock_torque].
